<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914734_theRebbe_896" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914734_theRebbe_896__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the superiority of baalei teshuvah over tzaddikim is due to their service being with greater strength because of their prior distance, and questions why healing is needed after peace is made for the distant one.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And behold, the reason that the level of the baalei teshuvah is greater than the level of the tzaddikim is</t>
    <t s="1">(as brought in the maamar)</t>
    <t s="2">because the service of the baalei teshuvah is with greater strength.</t>
    <t s="3">And the maamar clarifies,</t>
    <t s="4">that this—that the service of the baalei teshuvah is with greater strength—is because of the distance,</t>
    <t s="5">since initially they were distant from G‑dliness,</t>
    <t s="6">and why should their level be greater than the level of the tzaddikim who were always close to G‑dliness?</t>
    <t s="7">Also, one must understand</t>
    <t s="8">(as the maamar clarifies)</t>
    <t s="9">this—that after it says “Peace, peace to the far and to the near,” the verse continues, “said Hashem, and I will heal him,”</t>
    <t s="10">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="11">since even the distant one has become near and there is peace for the distant one,</t>
    <t s="12">why is healing needed?</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the connection of the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah to Ein Sof and the drawing down of Ein Sof into them is through Torah, Avodah, and Gemilus Chasadim, which correspond to thought, speech, and action.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And to explain this, the maamar first cites the verse</t>
    <t s="2">“Everyone who is called by My name and for My glory I created him, I formed him, even I made him,”</t>
    <t s="3">for “I created him, I formed him, even I made him” are the three worlds Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="4">in which all worlds are included.</t>
    <t s="5">And it explains,</t>
    <t s="6">that the connection of the worlds to Ein Sof</t>
    <t s="7">(from below upward)</t>
    <t s="8">and the drawing down of Ein Sof into the worlds</t>
    <t s="9">(from above downward)</t>
    <t s="10">is through the Torah.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is “and for My glory I created him, I formed him, even I made him,”</t>
    <t s="12">that the connection of the worlds to Ein Sof and the drawing down of Ein Sof into the worlds is through “My glory,”</t>
    <t s="13">for there is no glory except Torah.</t>
    <t s="14">And the maamar continues,</t>
    <t s="15">that the connection of the worlds to Ein Sof and the drawing down of Ein Sof into the worlds is through three matters,</t>
    <t s="16">Torah, Avodah, and Gemilus Chasadim.</t>
    <t s="17">And the reason for this is,</t>
    <t s="18">for the three worlds Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah are thought, speech, and action,</t>
    <t s="19">therefore,</t>
    <t s="20">the connection of the three worlds to Ein Sof and likewise the drawing down of Ein Sof into the three worlds,</t>
    <t s="21">is through Torah, Avodah, and Gemilus Chasadim,</t>
    <t s="22">for these three matters are thought, speech, and action</t>
    <t s="23">[Avodah – thought,</t>
    <t s="24">Torah – speech,</t>
    <t s="25">and Gemilus Chasadim – action].</t>
    <t s="26">And what is said “and for My glory I created him, I formed him, even I made him,”</t>
    <t s="27">that “My glory” is Torah,</t>
    <t s="28">it is,</t>
    <t s="29">because even the two matters of Avodah and Gemilus Chasadim must be in accordance with Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the descent of the soul through the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah is for the purpose of its service in Torah, Avodah, and Gemilus Chasadim, through which it returns and is elevated to its source in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And similarly regarding the creation of man and the descent of his soul below,</t>
    <t s="1">that the descent is through the three worlds Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="2">“You</t>
    <t s="3">created her</t>
    <t s="4">(Beriah)</t>
    <t s="5">You formed her</t>
    <t s="6">(Yetzirah)</t>
    <t s="7">You breathed her into me</t>
    <t s="8">(Asiyah),”</t>
    <t s="9">that the connection of man to Ein Sof and the drawing down of Ein Sof into man are through his service in the three matters of Torah, Avodah, and Gemilus Chasadim.</t>
    <t s="10">And through this, the return and restoration of the soul to its source in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof is effected.</t>
    <t s="11">For in addition to this, that it ascends to the level of “pure is she”</t>
    <t s="12">(Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="13">as it was before the descent of “You created her”),</t>
    <t s="14">it ascends to its first source in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="15">and “the spirit shall return to G‑d Who gave it.”</t>
    <t s="16">That is,</t>
    <t s="17">that even as it is below,</t>
    <t s="18">clothed in a physical body,</t>
    <t s="19">it is united with Him, blessed be He, in absolute unity, just as it was included in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof</t>
    <t s="20">(before the descent of “and He breathed”).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
